0.8.0.title: alpha
lead: The wonders can be found and are worth finding: the worlds' people point at them, every relic gives its world's gift, a group shares the reliquary, and the Journal draws a map of every world.
blocks: The people of every world speak of its wonder: one greeting in two, while its relic is still to be found, they say in which direction it stands and how far. The Journal's world card keeps what they said.
Every relic gives, besides its heart, a gift of its world: the relics of Worlds 1, 2, 5 and 7 make Toxin, Heat, Noise and the loss of breath a quarter slower (
has all four rules); the others give luck in chests, faster attacks, safe falls, speed, less knockback or faster mining. The ten together add 4 armour.
A reliquary opened by one member of a group gives its relic to every member standing within 24 blocks, straight into their inventory.
is rebuilt as a great wax candle in a ring of open arches, and the
as a giant lying on its back, face to the sky, moss grown over it.

A map of every world, from the world's card: the ground walked through inked in the world's colour, the places found drawn by role (people, combat, exploration, story, secret, wonder), the player as a small doll, and a legend of what has been found.
Each of the twenty lesser biomes has its own variation of its world's theme, in the same mode, with its own tempo and lead instrument.
New sounds for the reliquary opening and refusing a key, for a relic taken in, and a quiet air near a wonder.
The game tests check that every world raises its wonder inside the group's parcel and that a relic eases its world's rule.
The CI's game runs on Minecraft 26.3 start at last: it gets a software Vulkan device beside Mesa's OpenGL.

0.7.0.title: alpha
lead: Every world hides a wonder with a sealed reliquary that only a key from another world opens, the Journal gives every world a card of its items, the
has more to find before the first boss, and every block, item, tool and armour piece is repainted.
blocks: Wonders and the keys between the worlds
One wonder per world, rarer than any structure and seen from afar: the

At its heart a sealed reliquary, and beside it a vault chest with the world's cross key. A cross key never opens its own world's reliquary: the key of World n opens the reliquary of World (n + 3) mod 10 + 1, so the worlds have to be travelled back and forth. The wrong key leaves it shut and says which key it waits for.
Opened, a reliquary gives its world's relic, once per player. Each relic used adds one heart of health for good, ten relics ten hearts.
Every world has a card: its items and how each one is made (at which station), dropped (by which creature or boss), mined or found (in which chests). Open it by clicking the world on the Worlds page.
The Artisan's old cabin, with notes of his in the chests; the Peddler's stall; a giant doll fallen from somewhere higher. They are found above ground, before the first boss.
Every block, item, tool and armour piece is repainted in Minecraft's own manner: hard tones, clustered materials, lit edges and a shape of its own for every material.
The CI's first steps and whole-game runs are bounded in time, and their logs are kept even when they fail.

0.5.2.title: alpha
lead: The fights close in and hit harder, the bosses break as they weaken, the worlds' people speak, and the interface wears the mod's colours from the title screen to the tooltips.
blocks: A lair's portcullis drops row by row over the chamber's doorway when its boss wakes, and an altar arena's arch is barred while its rim burns with the world's light. Both open when the boss falls, or after 20 seconds with nobody inside, and close again behind the first one back.
A boss breaking into its later phases shows glowing cracks of its world's colour, more after the second.
A heavy or critical blow jolts the attacker's camera a little (comfort slider); the worlds' weapons spray their world's matter where they land and ring with the world's sound on a heavy hit.
A boss's relics fall where it fell and stay there, or at the nearest fighter's feet when it fell over the void.
The worlds' people greet a player who comes near in a speech bubble over their head, with a line that knows whether the boss of their world has fallen (the Peddler: how far down the group has gone).
The open worlds have skies of their own: a dark moon behind the spores, a full moon in the storm, an upside-down sky with stars by day in
, a starry sky over the sea, no stars in the Workshop.
A trophy doll won in the Trials rides on its owner's shoulder.
Matriochka items show their world, rarity and souls as pixel icons under their name.
Matriochka advancements are announced on the mod's own lacquer card.
The Journal's Worlds page shows the worlds nested as dolls and what has been gathered of each: pages, hidden doll, rite and boss.
The title screen shows a row of nesting dolls and the mod's version; a dive's loading screen stays dark under the doll's outline.
photographs the title screen, a tooltip, a toast, a greeting, a trophy on a shoulder, the Journal's map and
's sky; the playthrough checks every stage closes and opens again.

lead: Every boss now has a bar of its own and a proper end, and diving into a world is a moment of its own.
blocks: Every boss bar is drawn for its boss and its world, in pixel art on Minecraft's grid: runed stone pillars for the

Each gauge is the boss's own matter, animated: stone blocks, toxic sludge, molten metal, soul fire, a lightning arc, a dark that swallows light, a mirrored gauge emptying from both ends, deep water, the four seasons, a heartbeat, red lacquer. The damage just taken lingers as a pale trail, each phase is a notch, the name flashes on a hit, and the ends of the bar come alive.
Every boss comes out of its shell when summoned: folded and small, it swells, rears up and roars, with a burst of its world's particles.

A fallen boss folds back into its doll: two rings of gold close on it, its name is sealed on a card, and its relics fall from a column of light once the doll has closed. A boss unloaded before that still leaves its relics.
closes the screen on a doll-shaped iris in the world's colour while the camera plunges, and the iris opens again on the other side; the
runs it the other way. With cinematics off (comfort options), a plain fade.
's grid taps when a piece is set on it, rattles when a drawer lays a pattern out and chimes when a recipe forms.
summons every boss and photographs its awakening, its bar and its defeat.

blocks: still grows from a Seed planted on tilled

A rite site shows its object, puffs smoke while it waits and tells the player nearby what it still lacks. Feeding it still leans its world calm or wild. Each object keeps its item id (seed_2 to seed_10), so saves, recipes and quests carry over.
The bosses of Worlds 1 to 9 no longer drop World Soil; the Guardian still leaves the four soils

The thirteen stations are sculpted 3D models that face the player who places them, with fitted shapes and moving parts: the matrix over the workbench, the rank medal, the soul wisps, the vat's bubbles, the jailer's key, the forge's arc, the dark crystal, the inverter's ring, the press ram, the pendulum and clock hands, the anchor's stones, the loom shuttle. Their lit parts glow in the dark; the HD pack has 32 x 32 materials.
Every station screen has its own layout and material: jars on two shelves (
), plates in two arcs over an anvil (

). A bar under the pieces shows the recipe under the cursor, and the niche holds a live instrument per station: thermometer, capacitor cells, an eye that opens in the dark, a depth gauge, a clock, a seismograph.

is a 3 x 3 crafting table: every recipe made there has a pattern built from its exact cost, the result is taken like a crafted item, and its drawers fill the grid from the inventory like a recipe book.
Every boss is heard before it is seen: a breath, a growl or a hum in its world's colour.

Each rite sounds like its world while it works (embers, a turning key, a storm, a breath, glass, water, leaves, grinding rock, wooden doll halves) and opens its world with a swell in the world's own key.

An Items page lists every item and block as an inventory, with nested dolls to pick a world, a search, and a sheet for each one: its recipe drawn slot by slot (the workbench's as a real 3 x 3 grid), the station that makes it, where it comes from, what it is used for and, for a station, everything it makes. Every ingredient and use opens its own sheet.
Recipes across the site are drawn the same way, with the stations' 3D renders and vanilla ingredient icons.
photographs every station model, the row by day and night, and every station screen;

0.4.3.title: alpha
lead: Each world's rule meter now reads like the vanilla HUD: a row of ten icons above the hunger bar.
blocks: Each world's rule meter is now a vanilla status row instead of a gauge bar in the plaque: ten 9 x 9 pixel-art icons right above the hunger bar, filling in halves like the shanks (5% a half icon). A drop that fills with poison (

), a flame (2), an hourglass toward the halls' next move (3), a lightning bolt charging up to the next gust (4), a bell for noise (5), a feather toward the columns' next turn (6), brass portholes of breath and, with a snorkel helmet, small air tanks (7), a leaf in the season's colours as the season turns (8), a cracked stone toward the next tremor (9), the zone's own meter in

and an eye for Obsession (World 0). The containers flash white when the meter jumps, the icons tremble when it climbs fast, and near the threshold they shake like low hearts and pulse in their danger colours (steady with Flashes off).
The row is a Fabric status bar: it stacks above the air bubbles under water and above a mount's hearts, other mods' bars stack around it, and it hides with the vanilla bars (F1, creative, spectator).
The plaque keeps the world's medallion, its name and its rule, the Doll of Life and the souls; the Gauge patterns option now draws its stripes and crosshatching on the row's icons.
The server syncs the progress of the timed rules (the halls' move, the gusts, the gravity columns, the season and the zone a player stands in within
) so the client can draw their meters.

photographs the row in every world at 0, 35, 55 and 90% at GUI scales 2 and 3, under water with the air bubbles, with a snorkel's tank and breath, with full armor and absorption hearts, riding a horse, with the patterns, with F1 and in creative, the plaque with the first-steps card and a trial.

0.4.2.title: alpha
lead: The mod's traders get a painted market stall, and every ending now closes on a recap of the cycle.
blocks: The mod's peoples trade at a painted market stall instead of the villager screen (the people of each world, the Doll Peddler, the travelling merchants and the black market): a ledger of every offer on parchment with its stock and the karma's discount or markup, a plum "under the counter" section for the black market's goods, sold-out lines stamped, the trader's plaque with its world's medallion, the kind of trader, a travelling merchant's time left and the karma, the counter with the selected trade and the inventory tray. Each boss's 3D viewer plays its real attacks, named in English and French, as one move (wind-up, strike, recover), plus its phase change and fall; the bosses page shows every attack's wind-up and strike in game, with a link to the attack in 3D.

0.4.1.title: alpha
lead: The kneel at the end calms the whole room, the Trials and talent screens and the new structures are fixed after a look at every one of them, talents are balanced against the design, and the Matriochka Pack has its own Modrinth project.
blocks: now models the talents: for every class and world, the talents open on arrival, applied as the game applies them, on top of the design player. A class's whole tree may move the hits to kill a creature, the hits you survive and the length of a solo boss fight by a quarter at most (report:

Berserker talents lowered: Giantkiller and Shell Splitter 6% + 12% -> 3% + 5% against bosses, Cleaver 5% -> 4%, Bloodied and Red Mist 15% + 25% -> 10% + 12%, Opener and Finisher 20% -> 10%, Quick Arm and Flurry 5% + 10% -> 3% + 4% attack speed. With the weapon's +58% at level 5, the tree added up to +101% against a boss and cut the solo fights of Worlds 9 and 10 by 40%; now +83% and 24%.

Guardian: the bulwark gives health and toughness instead of armor (Stout +1 max health, Plated and Unbroken +0.5 toughness, Last Wall 10%), Broad Back and Hearty +1 max health, Lacquer Skin 2 absorption. Near the armor cap every point counts so much that the tree made a
player survive 5.3 strong boss blows instead of 3; now 3.8.
Survivor: Thick Skin and Iron Heart +1 and +2 max health, Stubborn and Never Down 10% and 15%. Prowler: First Cut 10%, Stalker and Assassin 10% and 20% while sneaking.

The ending's kneel calms the whole room: the creatures the Artisan's Shadow called in let go of the kneeling player, freeze in loose thread and unravel into thread and gold dust a second later, and the blows already thrown fade. They no longer knock the player off the carpet.
The new structures of the Ember Veins (
) stand on a cave floor under the rock roof; they were placed on the roof, above the build limit, and never built.
The caravans, circles, outposts and bastions no longer stand on a pillar of foundation in the middle of a lake or a sea.
is held like a shield and raised across the body while it blocks (it was held like a flat item); its flare bursts in gold sparks in front of the bearer instead of white rods in the player's face.

The trial clock sits under the boss bars instead of over them, scales with the HUD size comfort option, and the boss attack subtitles keep below it. The countdown is drawn large in the middle of the screen, a gilt figure each second.

The Talent cabinet: the talent's name sits on the plaque between the sprigs, the description, cost and reason shrink together to fit the red panel in any language, branch and class names shrink instead of being cut, the tree is centred on its panel and the Forget button is a full lacquer button.
The Trials book and the Journal no longer overlap wrapped text with what follows it; the Trials board's empty line wraps on the page.
Rebuilding a Gauntlet stage no longer drops the previous stage's carpets and banners at the players' feet.

Surges use their world's own particles (spores, embers, cold dust, storm sparks, shadow wisps, mirror shards, bubbles, petals, grit, thread), the warlord's name and its wave's warning are written in gold instead of an unreadable dark red, the harpoon draws its line to its catch, and the
's tremor cracks the ground in rings of crumbs and grit.
The harpoon line is only drawn while its thrower is in the same world and within 48 blocks.
A first-steps guide that jumps to its end (progression given by command, a group ahead, an ending already seen) no longer shows its goodbye card, and the card never draws during a trial.
photographs the Trials, their stages in ten worlds, the HUD clock, the Trials and Talent screens in English and German, the new gear in hand and in use, the world events and the ten new structures (

blocks: Trials, open once you have seen an ending: a rush per world (two waves of its creatures, the second led by its elites, then its boss) and the Gauntlet of the eleven bosses, fought against the clock on a lacquered stage inside the Refuge doll, painted for each world. . Falling carries you out instead of killing you.
A trial clock on the HUD (green under par), best times per player and per group, and a server-wide board of the ten best groups per trial, in the new Trials book and with
. The first win of each trial gives its Trophy Doll and a title; finishing under par gives Swift Hand. Titles can be worn from the Trials book, quest titles included.

World events while you are in a world: invasions (three waves, the last led by a glowing warlord, a reward chest at the end), a surge of each world's rule (twice as strong for two minutes, with its own effect and particles:

, Magma Surge, Lockdown, Tempest, Blackout, Gravity Storm, Crushing Current, Season Rush, Great Quake, Unravelling) and a travelling merchant per world with special trades. A boss bar follows each event. Never in peaceful; frequency and weights in
, the three weights). Operators can start one with

: three branches of four talents per class, bought with souls and, for the last two of a branch, Shell Shards, opened by your group's progression. A class's talents act while you wear or hold its gear. A new cabinet screen with the six trees, tooltips for every talent and a Forget button that gives back half the souls.

One more structure per world: the Gatherers' and Ephemeral Caravans, the Ember, Hushed and Restless Circles, the
, the Sky, Hanging and Thimble Outposts, each decorated in its world's materials, with its loot.

spreads its arms like walls, the

paints a new face) and its own fall, which now plays out for two seconds instead of the vanilla tip-over.

New hand-painted textures for the items and blocks you see most, in the vanilla style (outlines, three to four tones lit from the top left, warm highlights and cool shadows): the ten hidden dolls, the
and the other dolls, the eleven cores, the ten Seeds, every armor piece and world weapon, the four snorkel helmets, the Scroll, Journal and pages, the four boss offerings, the World Soils, the
and every face of the thirteen stations. Each world's objects share its palette and glyph.
The lit parts of the stations and the

(petals, pollen, leaves or snow), rust haze in

's cold fog is darker than its stone, so its halls read at a corridor's length;
stays black, but a lantern now reads across a cavern (its fog closes in from 4 to 30 blocks).

Eighteen new particles (spores, embers, cold dust, chain glints, lightning sparks, shadow wisps, deep motes, mirror shards, bubbles, petals, pollen, leaves, snowflakes, grit, rust, thread scraps, fluff, gold dust). Matriochka HD: an optional resource pack with the same textures at 32 x 32, attached to each release.

Station automation: every station with recipes now works with hoppers. A station keeps one recipe, the last one crafted there by hand or the one picked with the new gilded funnel on its drawer. Ingredients go in from the top and the sides (each ingredient has its own slots, anything else is refused), the result comes out from below, and a comparator reads how full the station is. Each station keeps its condition: heat for the
fed into its fuel slot), darkness, deep water, dawn and dusk; the
waits for a ripe brew and the
makes one batch per lock pattern entered. The
stay manual. Breaking a station drops its buffer.

on purpose: a player of the owning group outside can sneak and use it with empty hands to help those inside (creatures stunned and thrown off their feet for 3 seconds, a boss staggered and open), or strike it with the new

Boss introductions: letterbox bars, the camera turning toward the boss with a slow push-in, and a framed title card with the boss's name and title.
A title card the first time you enter each world, with its rule medallion and a line about its law.
Boss phase breaks freeze-frame with a flash and the shell's number; heavy boss blows,
's quake and a trembling World Block nearby shake the camera.
The endings' crawl is framed by letterbox bars.

Adaptive music: a danger theme while creatures hunt you, the boss themes during fights, a heartbeat at low health or breath, and stings for a structure, a Journal page or a quest; themes fade into one another and the world theme comes back soon after.
, a small lacquered card under the HUD plaque shows the next of ten steps (read the Scroll, find the Guardian's Sanctuary, wake and defeat the Guardian, place the

Matriochka is translated into Spanish, German and Brazilian Portuguese: every name, the interface, quests, achievements, the Scroll, the fifty Journal pages, endings, credits and subtitles. A string missing from a language shows in English.
